title: Shiliao Bencao · Section on daily diet (食疗)
source: 《食疗本草》, Tang dynasty, c. 8th century CE
provenance: Public domain classical Chinese text. English summary is Nadi's editorial paraphrase; the original Chinese is preserved in the citation chain.
summary_en: Food is prescribed by nature, not by nature alone. A dish that suits one body may not suit another at another hour. Consistency over intensity — a small, gentle, repeatable change is preferred over a dramatic, unsustainable one.
summary_zh: 食疗之要，在于顺性而行；一人之食，未必适他时。贵乎恒常，不贵骤变。

title: Shiliao Bencao · Daily rhythm and sleep
source: 《食疗本草》, Tang dynasty, c. 8th century CE
provenance: Public domain classical Chinese text. English summary is Nadi's editorial paraphrase.
summary_en: Rise with the light, eat light at dusk. Sleep is not for recovering from exhaustion but for preventing it. A body that is moved in the morning requires less from the night.
summary_zh: 日升而起，黄昏而食宜少。寝非为补倦，乃为防倦。晨动则夜需少。

title: Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing · Overview
provenance: Public domain classical Chinese pharmacopoeia, 365 herbs classified into three grades. Nadi uses only the structural framework, not the specific herb claims.
summary_en: The upper grade tonifies and may be taken long-term without harm. The middle grade corrects excess and deficiency. The lower grade treats acute conditions but may not be taken long-term. This three-tier classification is a durable idea of risk-bounded use.
summary_zh: 上品无毒，多服久服不伤人；中品有补有泻；下品主病，多有毒，不可久服。
